research_program: Copy-aware Paged KV management and adaptive execution for commodity single-GPU llama.cpp serving

claims.question: When does 128-bit vectorization reduce the cost of snapshot-preserving KV Remap?
claims.hypothesis: With identical descriptors and snapshot semantics on the locked environment, uint4 Gather/Scatter reduces GPU time relative to scalar Remap for aligned FP16 KV, and the paired median improvement is non-increasing across 1, 4, 16, and 32 remapped blocks.
independent_variables: scalar versus uint4 Remap
remapped block count: 1, 4, 16, 32
alignment and scalar-tail fraction
confounders: GPU clock, temperature, and WDDM scheduling
claims.mechanism: Each aligned vector thread moves eight FP16 elements through one uint4 load/store. H2 Nsight Systems traces show equal scalar/vector launch counts and shorter aligned-small vector kernel duration, ruling out fewer launches as the cause; the misaligned scalar-lane fallback reverses the effect. Instruction, cache, occupancy, and hardware-bandwidth attribution remain prospective until NCU counters are available.
falsification: Any preregistered block count has paired median GPU regression above 3%.
No preregistered block count reaches 10% paired median GPU improvement.
Paired median improvement is not non-increasing across the locked 1, 4, 16, and 32 block sequence.
The vector path changes output, violates snapshot semantics, or produces sanitizer errors.
Production application evidence records no vectorized bytes while claiming that the path is used.
observed_results: Twenty paired alternating-order trials measured 53.33%, 48.89%, 3.13%, and 1.87% median GPU improvement for 1, 4, 16, and 32 blocks.
The real application journey recorded 5,603,330 vectorized Remap bytes.
These results are operator-level evidence and do not establish end-to-end serving acceleration.
scope_limits: RTX 4050 Laptop GPU, sm_89, Windows WDDM
FP16 KV with 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, 16-token blocks
KV movement operator only; not Paged Decode Attention
claims.negative_result_policy: Retain regressions by block count, alignment, and fallback fraction; do not average them into a positive headline.

claims.question: Under which workload and layout regimes does explicit KV movement materially affect decode service outcomes?
claims.hypothesis: Explicit KV movement becomes material as moved bytes, fragmentation, shared-prefix COW, and memory pressure increase, but scheduler-induced queueing can dominate or reverse the operator-level effect.
independent_variables: context length and moved KV bytes
fragmentation and overlap class
prefix sharing and COW frequency
batch shape, arrival process, and memory pressure
dependent_metrics: TTFT, TPOT/TBT, queue latency, request P95, and throughput
resident sequence capacity and fallback count
confounders: GPU power, clock, and thermal state
claims.mechanism: More explicit movement consumes device bandwidth and launches, while fragmentation and snapshot semantics determine whether Direct is legal; request scheduling can amplify or hide this cost through queue structure.
falsification: Profiler evidence shows KV movement is immaterial in every preregistered high-copy or high-pressure regime.
Reducing movement does not change kernel time, admissible capacity, or request outcomes beyond uncertainty in any regime.
Apparent request gains occur without a corresponding scheduler or CUDA mediator.
observed_results: Four preregistered regimes produced 160 no-profiler paired observations and four successful Nsight Systems traces.
Aligned 1-block vectorization improved CUDA-event time by a paired median 57.10% (95% CI 38.51% to 57.14%), while aligned 16/32-block cases were neutral under the 10% materiality gate.
The misaligned 1-block layout was a retained counterexample: vectorization regressed CUDA-event time by 137.94% (95% CI 137.84% to 140.55% regression) and end-to-end time by 113.02%.
Scalar and vectorized paths each launched 10 profiled kernels per regime, ruling out reduced launch count as the cause of the aligned-small gain.

A separate three-pair real-service experiment linked 72 deterministic requests across six trial/mode server processes to scheduler counters, KV actions, PID-filtered Nsight Systems kernels, and TTFT; every runtime KV launch count exactly matched NSYS.

In that service run, forced CacheFlow changed decisions by +20, prefill chunks by +30, prefill tokens by -86, KV launches by +0, copy bytes by +10,518,500, and CUDA-event time by -1.040 ms; paired median TTFT P95 worsened by 126.932 ms while Engine execute also increased by 146,493 us. The profiler replay contained 42 PID-filtered custom KV launches. This run closed the causal linkage but did not reproduce the earlier execute/TTFT sign reversal.

Nsight Compute counters remain unavailable because the installed profiler reported driver incompatibility and ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM; memory-bound, roofline, occupancy, and hardware-DRAM-byte claims remain prohibited.
scope_limits: Single RTX 4050 Laptop GPU
Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct serving slice
Nsight Systems kernel/copy/synchronization timeline is available; Nsight Compute hardware counters are not
No occupancy, roofline, hardware DRAM byte, or memory-bound claim until NCU evidence exists
claims.negative_result_policy: Publish regimes where non-KV compute or queueing dominates and narrow the research question instead of relabeling noise as a gain.

claims.question: When is restricted Paged Decode Attention preferable to Direct or explicit KV Remap?
claims.hypothesis: Direct page-table reads can avoid materialization bytes and improve capacity or latency only beyond a context, fragmentation, or reuse frontier; indirect addressing and online-softmax overhead may make it slower for short or contiguous cases.
independent_variables: Direct, Remap, or Paged Decode Attention action
context length, page size, and physical fragmentation
batch size and GQA shape
prefix reuse and resident sequence count
dependent_metrics: attention output error versus contiguous oracle
CUDA-event kernel time and device bytes
peak KV memory and admissible batch
TTFT, TPOT/TBT, request P95, and throughput
confounders: different attention math, masking, or precision
layout conversion outside the timed region
claims.mechanism: Paged Decode Attention removes full-cache materialization but adds block-table lookup, irregular memory access, masking, online softmax, and reduction costs; the winning action depends on avoided bytes and available concurrency.
falsification: The restricted kernel fails the numerical oracle or memory-safety checks.
It is neither non-inferior in latency nor beneficial in resident capacity in every preregistered regime.
Any measured gain disappears when layout conversion and warm-up are controlled.
The implementation silently falls back while metrics claim Paged execution.
observed_results: The restricted K1 CUDA kernel directly reads non-contiguous physical pages and produces FP32 attention output; independent CPU and contiguous-CUDA oracles cover Qwen2.5-0.5B 14/2/D64 and Qwen2.5-7B geometry 28/4/D128 with GQA ratio 7 and page size 16.
Every timed regime first passed an independent CPU FP32 paged-attention oracle; the maximum absolute CUDA output error was 3.6e-8.

The 0.5B 16-token regime was neutral; its 17-token regime showed a noisy +22.87% median improvement with a 0.00% to 47.08% interval that did not establish a stable material win. Every medium/long regime regressed by 10.41% to 13.05%.
At context 1024 and batch 1, the 0.5B shape regressed 13.05% (95% CI 12.91% to 13.12%) and the 7B kernel shape regressed 11.59% (95% CI 11.37% to 11.78%).

The long-context batch-1 versus batch-4 regression gaps were only 0.84 and 1.18 percentage points, so the preregistered split-K trigger did not fire; the at-least-3% long-context regression rule selected K2 GQA KV reuse as the next unimplemented hypothesis.

The formal environment is an RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (compute capability 8.9) with 6141 MiB total memory; per-regime input/output/workspace accounting is retained and the maximum benchmark device allocation was 16,864,272 bytes.

Four method-isolated Nsight Systems captures each contain exactly five matching launches. Nsight Compute reported driver incompatibility and ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, so memory-bound, occupancy, and hardware-DRAM-byte explanations are prohibited.
scope_limits: Qwen2.5, FP16 Q/K/V, FP32 output, GQA, head dimensions 64 and 128
Single-token decode and 16-token pages
Single RTX 4050 Laptop GPU; unsupported shapes fail closed in the prototype
The D128 result is model-faithful kernel geometry only, not end-to-end 7B serving evidence
No production dispatch, capacity benefit, or request-level latency claim in Issue #5
claims.negative_result_policy: Report the losing regions and capacity/latency trade-off; a slower kernel with a measured capacity benefit is not rewritten as a latency win.

claims.question: Can an explainable cost model safely select among KV execution actions better than a fixed rule?
claims.hypothesis: A model using measurable movement, fragmentation, reuse, memory-pressure, and compute features can reduce matched-workload regret relative to the fixed rule while bounding wrong enables and decision overhead.
independent_variables: fixed rule versus analytical, table-driven, learned, or hybrid policy
workload distribution and distribution shift
available action set and safety thresholds
dependent_metrics: TTFT, TPOT/TBT, request P95, throughput, and memory pressure
confounders: trace leakage between training and evaluation
claims.mechanism: No single action minimizes cost across copy legality, bytes, fragmentation, memory pressure, and decode work; an uncertainty-aware policy should choose only when predicted benefit exceeds risk and overhead.
falsification: The policy exceeds preregistered matched-workload regret or upstream-regression gates.
Decision overhead removes the selected action's benefit.
The policy continues harmful actions after a registered distribution shift.
A fixed rule matches or beats it across all held-out regimes within uncertainty.
observed_results: The v1.0.0 replay is superseded because it used client HTTP round-trip latency instead of the registered internal complete-action boundary and evaluated a different Ridge contract; it remains under results/research/superseded for audit only.

The v1.1.0 replay is also superseded because it used synthetic canonical model inputs, resampled decisions rather than trace clusters, lacked preregistered balanced collection order, and reported CUDA synchronization from a literal rather than a source-bound audit.

The v1.2.0 replay is superseded because it did not retain raw Prometheus evidence, reused one Recompute observation across two regimes, ignored physical observation order in Ridge replay, and described a lexical synchronization audit too strongly.

The v1.6.0 CUDA matched-workload replay collected 120 new trace-isolated groups with new collection and bootstrap seeds, split chronologically into 60 fit, 20 calibration, and 40 evaluation traces, and hash-bound 600 raw Prometheus/response observations.

Risk-budgeted D3 made 24 of 80 held-out decisions away from H0. Its cumulative regret was 2.082 ms versus H0's 42.590 ms, a 95.1% reduction; P95 regret was 0 versus 3.169 ms; and the matched-workload trace-cluster mean-regret delta 95% CI was -0.7232 to -0.3069 ms. The artifact's paired_trace_cluster field is a legacy machine name, not a formal same-hot-process Trial Pair.

D3 had one harmful decision: 1.25% of all 80 eligible decisions, the preregistered denominator, and 4.17% of its 24 actual switches. Both observed replay proportions were below 5%; no population-level harmful-rate confidence-bound claim is made. Its 41.480 ms total measured gain exceeded 0.972 ms total measured harm, so every v1.6 acceptance gate passed.
D1 and D2 made no held-out switch. T1 reached 18.061 ms cumulative regret with one harmful decision. The v1.4 and v1.5 negative results remain retained and are not overwritten by v1.6.

The four action observations come from independent fixed-mode server processes, so action and process remain confounded and no action-causal claim is made. The v1.6 overhead benchmark recorded p99 0.900 us, decision/action ratio p99 0.0874%, and zero heap allocations on the existing bounded production chooser seam. D3 remains offline and requires a same-process monitored canary before online enablement.
scope_limits: The unified policy currently executes H0; v1.6 justifies a monitored D3 canary but does not silently enable D3 online.

Issue #6 production-complete evidence covers Direct, CUDA-managed pinned-host swap, transactional host swap, and Recompute. Issue #7 separately added real Remap and a restricted Paged llama_decode adapter without rewriting the Issue #6 replay.
No reinforcement-learning claim
Held-out evaluation is restricted to the available single-GPU workload matrix
claims.negative_result_policy: Keep the fixed rule when it is statistically indistinguishable or safer; publish misprediction regimes and fallback behavior.

claims.question: Can a scheduling decision change CUDA work yet harm request latency despite reducing aggregate engine execution time?
claims.hypothesis: Policy interventions affect request outcomes through scheduler shape and CUDA KV work, and phase aggregates are insufficient because changed batching and queue order can reverse TTFT.
independent_variables: forced upstream versus forced CacheFlow policy
paired fresh-process trial order
dependent_metrics: KV launches, copied bytes, and CUDA-event time
claims.mechanism: More chunks and changed batch order alter queue waiting while adding KV work; aggregate execute duration omits how work is distributed across requests.
falsification: The intervention changes no scheduling decision.
Scheduling changes occur without a material CUDA mediator.
CUDA changes occur without a material request-level outcome.
The effect vanishes under paired trials and is attributable only to sampling noise.
observed_results: Three paired Latin interventions recorded +13 CacheFlow decisions, +23 prefill chunks, -354 prefill tokens, +2 custom KV launches, +20,066,300 copied bytes, and +0.808 ms CUDA-event time.
Engine execute aggregate decreased by 11,446 us while TTFT P95 worsened by 85.61 ms.
The current 100 ms activity sampling is not an Nsight kernel census.
scope_limits: Three paired trials on one laptop GPU
Causal chain for the tested forced-policy workload only
No occupancy, roofline, or universal scheduler conclusion
claims.negative_result_policy: Treat harmful TTFT as a primary result and require future policies to explain or avoid it; never substitute phase aggregates for request metrics.

claims.question: Can the restricted paged decode kernel execute inside the real llama.cpp service path without correctness loss, and does it pass the preregistered production promotion gate?
claims.hypothesis: For the registered Qwen2.5-0.5B short-context envelope, the production Paged path preserves exact deterministic output and does not regress client P95 by more than 5% versus Direct.
independent_variables: explicit Direct versus Paged action override
seeded AB/BA fresh-process pair order
dependent_metrics: client latency P95 and paired latency effect
PID-filtered production Paged CUDA kernel launches
confounders: fresh-process startup and Windows scheduling noise
short context where launch overhead dominates
single laptop GPU and one model shape
claims.mechanism: The graph consumes the physical KV block table directly through a restricted CUDA online-softmax kernel; capability and layout checks occur before KV mutation, while a separate no-profiler paired service experiment decides promotion.
falsification: Any paired response differs from Direct.
The Paged action falls back or fails to enter the production graph.
PID-filtered NSYS replay does not contain one Paged kernel launch per model layer.
Paged client P95 regresses by more than the preregistered 5% promotion limit.
observed_results: The v1.0 artifact is superseded because its five-token request did not cross a physical page boundary; it is retained under results/research/superseded for audit only.
All ten v1.1 AB/BA pairs used a measured 17-token cross-page context and produced exact matching content; Paged entered the production graph ten times with zero fallbacks.
A method-isolated PID-filtered NSYS replay recorded exactly 24 cacheflow_paged_decode_fattn_k1<64> launches, one per Qwen2.5-0.5B layer; profiler timing is non-primary.
Direct client latency was median/P95 16.054/27.354 ms and Paged was 21.404/29.210 ms. The paired Paged-minus-Direct median was +2.705 ms with a bootstrap 95% interval of -1.185 to +12.019 ms.
Paged P95 regressed by 6.78%, exceeding the preregistered +5% limit. Correctness passed, production promotion failed, and Paged remains opt-in and excluded from default policy selection.
scope_limits: Qwen2.5-0.5B, FP16 KV, D64, page 16, batch/query token 1, context no greater than 17, complete CUDA offload
One RTX 4050 Laptop GPU and Windows driver 561.19
No long-context, memory-capacity, larger-model, or universal latency claim
NSYS launch identity is mechanism evidence and its timing is not used for the primary latency result
claims.negative_result_policy: Keep Paged opt-in and fail closed when the promotion gate loses; preserve exact correctness and mechanism evidence without relabeling it as a speedup.

claims.question: Can a GQA-reusing K2 kernel replace the correct but slower K1 inside the restricted production Paged path?
claims.hypothesis: For the registered Qwen2.5-0.5B D64/GQA7/context-17-to-24 eight-token steady-state envelope, K2 preserves output, keeps unprofiled client median and P95 regression within 5%, and reduces equal-launch-count target-kernel duration by at least 20% relative to K1.
independent_variables: same-process K1 versus K2 kernel selector
seeded random K1-K2 or K2-K1 order within each pair
dependent_metrics: exact response content, production graph entries, and fallbacks
unprofiled client median/P95 and paired server prompt time
PID-isolated NSYS target-kernel identity, launches, and duration
confounders: Windows scheduling and localhost HTTP outliers
fresh serving process and GPU clock state
claims.mechanism: K2-T2 maps two query heads to two warps in one CTA, stages their shared GQA K/V once per tile so each KV head needs four loads instead of K1's seven, transposes shared K to avoid the token-read bank-conflict pattern, and uses warp reductions for stable softmax; the formal promotion is restricted to D64/GQA7/context 17 through 24.
falsification: Any K1/K2 output differs or either arm falls back.
Unprofiled K2 client median or P95 regresses by more than 5%.
PID-isolated NSYS target-kernel launch counts differ or K2 aggregate duration does not improve by at least 20%.
observed_results: Thirty steady-state pairs produced exact matching content, 300 production Paged graph entries, and zero fallbacks.
K1/K2 unprofiled client medians were 44.8794/41.4166 ms, a 7.72% K2 reduction; P95 values were 57.2525/55.8971 ms, a 2.37% reduction.

The paired K2-minus-K1 client median was -1.028 ms with a bootstrap 95% interval of [-5.095, 1.618] ms; promotion is bounded non-inferiority plus mechanism improvement, not a population-wide speedup claim.
PID-isolated NSYS recorded equal 24 target-kernel launches; aggregate duration was 0.438049 ms for K1 and 0.228225 ms for K2, a 47.90% reduction.
Failed v2.0/v2.1/v2.4/v2.5 and invalid v2.3/v2.6 artifacts remain retained. The v2.7 promotion is K2 over K1 only and does not reverse the failed Paged-over-Direct result.
scope_limits: Qwen2.5-0.5B, F32 Q, FP16 KV, D64, GQA ratio 7, page 16, batch 1, decode contexts 17 through 24, complete CUDA offload
One RTX 4050 Laptop GPU on Windows
No long-context, prefill, larger-model, Paged-over-Direct, or universal throughput claim
No hardware DRAM-byte, occupancy, bank-conflict-counter, or memory-bound claim because NCU counters remain unavailable
claims.negative_result_policy: Retain failed K1/K2 protocols and keep the Paged-over-Direct action boundary unchanged; do not promote unsupported shapes or contexts.
